review_notes: I read the whole file and looked at its simp lemmas and the simp attributes on definitions. I paid most attention to `eval_map_algebraMap` against `eval_map`, `aeval_monomial`, the `simps` lemmas on the `algEquiv*` definitions, `aevalTower_*`, `mapAlgHom` and `mapAlgEquiv`. I found no loops and no competing rules among them. In particular, `eval_map` is not simp, so it does not compete with `eval_map_algebraMap`. `aeval_algHom_apply` is used as a local simp lemma in about 15 places and also rewritten right-to-left in many others. Because the uses go in both directions, I did not recommend making it global. The one finding is the redundant `aeval_neg` and `aeval_sub`. It is minor and rests on the assumption that the generic `map_neg` and `map_sub` fire on `aeval x` applied to a negation or difference. I did not run Lean, so I could not confirm that. I did not look further for other lemmas that would make these two redundant.

findings.problem: `aeval_neg` and `aeval_sub` are tagged `@[simp]`, but their proofs are exactly the generic `map_neg` and `map_sub`. `aeval x` is an `AlgHom`, so those generic simp lemmas should already rewrite `aeval x (-p)` and `aeval x (p - q)` to the same normal forms. The two `@[simp]` attributes therefore probably add nothing to the default simp set. Other lemmas in this file follow the same pattern without `@[simp]`: `aeval_zero`, `aeval_add`, `aeval_one`, `aeval_mul` and `aeval_natCast` are plain `map_*` wrappers. So the simp tagging is inconsistent across this family. This rests on my reading and was not tested with Lean.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `aeval_neg` and `aeval_sub`, as for `aeval_add` and `aeval_mul`. Keep the lemmas as named rewrite lemmas, since other files cite them by name in `simp only`, for example `aeval_sub` in `Mathlib/FieldTheory/RatFunc/IntermediateField.lean`. Before doing so, check with the simpNF linter whether `map_neg` and `map_sub` really already fire on these terms.
findings.benefit: This gives a leaner simp set with one rule per normal form. It also makes the file consistent about which `aeval` lemmas are simp. `simp` behaviour should be unchanged if `map_neg` and `map_sub` already apply.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem aeval_add : aeval x (p + q) = aeval x p + aeval x q :=
  map_add _ _ _
